issues.description: Element: Animal.getName() and Animal.setName(). Problem statement (instructions) requires the name getter and setter to have protected visibility (problem_statement.md directs: "implement the name getter and setter with protected visibility"), but the solution implementation (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java) provides public methods getName() and setName(). This discrepancy can confuse students about the intended encapsulation level of Animal's API and whether subclasses should rely on protected access or external code may call these methods publicly.
issues.suggestedFix: Resolve the visibility mismatch. Either change the solution's Animal.getName() and Animal.setName() signatures to protected to match the exercise instructions, or update the problem statement/UML to specify public visibility for these methods so all artifacts are consistent. Ensure the template and any example usages (e.g., in Main or tests) reflect the chosen visibility.

issues.description: Element: Animal(String) constructor. The UML in the problem statement marks the constructor as protected (UML shows '#' visibility for Animal(String)), but the solution implementation (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java) declares the constructor as public. This inconsistency can mislead students about intended construction/access patterns for the abstract Animal class (whether instantiation by subclasses vs. broader package/public instantiation is intended).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor visibility consistent across artifacts. Either change the solution's Animal(String) constructor to protected to match the UML, or update the UML/problem statement to mark the constructor public if broader visibility was intended. Also update the template and any sample code to reflect the chosen constructor visibility.

issues.description: The problem statement requires the Animal name accessor methods to use protected visibility (note in problem_statement.md: "implement the name getter and setter with protected visibility"). In the solution, the methods are declared as public: public String getName() and public void setName(String) (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java). This mismatch between the required visibility (protected) and the implemented visibility (public) can confuse students about the expected access level for the Animal API and how encapsulation should be applied. Call sites in the solution (e.g., Pig.messageOnRide(), Seal.messageOnRide(), Goat.messageOnMilk()) use getName(), which would still be valid with protected visibility because they are in the same package/subclasses, but the inconsistency between the textual requirement and the actual implementation remains and may mislead students when implementing or grading.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the implementation with the problem statement by changing the Animal accessors to protected (e.g., change public String getName() to protected String getName() and public void setName(String) to protected void setName(String)). Alternatively, if public access was intentional, update the problem statement note to remove or change the protected-visibility requirement so students are not instructed to implement a different visibility than the provided solution.
